project.name: PokéScale
project.what: Browser game: resize a silhouetted Pokémon until it looks the right size next to a reference Pokémon on a shared ground line. 5 rounds, 5000 points, static, no backend.
project.remote: https://github.com/YheChen/PokemonSize (the origin URL still uses the old Pokemon-Size name, which GitHub redirects)
project.stack: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack) + React 19 + TypeScript 5 + Tailwind CSS 4, pnpm 10, Vitest 4, sharp 0.35
project.deploy: Vercel project yhechens-projects/pokescale, live at https://pokescale.vercel.app. Fully static prerender, no env vars, no serverless functions, no database. The GitHub app is authorised, so a push to master deploys production automatically; `vercel --prod` is only needed for an out-of-band deploy.

commands.dev: pnpm dev  (launch.json config 'pokescale' runs it on port 3210)
commands.verifiedMeans: pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build all clean, PLUS a manual browser pass (landing, 5 rounds, reveal, results, share, play-again) at 320 / 390 / 768 / 1440 widths in light and dark.

gotchas: SCALE CORRECTNESS IS THE TOP INVARIANT. Figures get an explicit pixel height plus a width from the sprite aspect ratio. Never use transform: scale() on a figure and never use object-fit: contain on the sprite; both would make the measured guess differ from the drawn size.
Sprites MUST stay alpha-cropped. The whole point of build-pokemon-assets.ts is that box height == visible Pokémon height. Swapping in raw PokéAPI artwork silently breaks every comparison.
referencePixelHeight must never depend on the round, or its size leaks the answer. It is min(stageHeight*0.38, usableWidth/(1+MAX_CLASSIC_RATIO), 300), and both terms are round-independent.

MAX_CLASSIC_RATIO (2.45) and REFERENCE_STAGE_FRACTION (0.38) are coupled: their product must stay under STAGE_HEADROOM (0.94) so a largest-legal target still fits. Raising the ratio ceiling shrinks the reference in every round. A sizing test asserts this.
generateGameRounds takes an optional `stage` and only emits pairs that fit it. Without it, rounds are still ratio-bounded but assume a generic stage.
Percentage heights need a definite parent: the stage chain is flex-1 + min-h-0 all the way down. An h-full child of an auto-height parent silently collapses (this bit once already).

The silhouette->colour CSS transition must only be attached to the colour variant. Attaching it to the silhouette makes the NEXT round fade in from full colour and briefly show the answer. The is also keyed by pokemon.id for the same reason.
eslint-config-next 16 ships native flat config, so import 'eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals' directly. FlatCompat + @eslint/eslintrc throws 'Converting circular structure to JSON'.
@next/next/no-img-element is deliberately disabled: next/image would re-encode and re-letterbox the normalized sprites, which is exactly what the pipeline exists to prevent.
sharp in this environment ignores png({palette:true}); palette quantization is a silent no-op, so PNG sizes are what they are (~40KB each).
React state is async: when testing via devtools, reading aria-valuenow synchronously after dispatching a keydown returns the OLD value. Wait a tick.
The browser automation harness could not deliver real key events to the page; keyboard handling was verified by dispatching KeyboardEvents and awaiting a tick.
House style: no em dashes anywhere, in UI copy, code comments or docs. Use commas, colons or a second sentence instead.
